title: Spherical cavity, radius 10 mm, with a concentric ceramic sphere (εr = 4) of radius 4 mm and, in the vacuum around it, a cylinder of εr = 1 holding a disc of εr = 1 of its own radius on its floor: the TM11 triplet
source: Two-layer spherical cavity (R. F. Harrington, Time-Harmonic Electromagnetic Fields, 1961, §6.10, extended to two layers; the roots computed by emcraft-theory, bessel::layered_sphere_resonances): bodies filled like the vacuum around them change nothing of the field, so the resonance is the loaded sphere's — if the regions meet node for node where the disc lies against its cylinder's wall from inside, along its side (one cylinder) and on its floor (one plane)
